EarthquakeFeatureCollection.title: EarthquakeFeatureCollection
EarthquakeFeatureCollection.description: A GeoJSON FeatureCollection of earthquakes: the wire frame both the summary feeds and the event query answer with.

metadata.title: FeedMetadata
metadata.description: About this answer, not about the earthquakes in it.

title.description: Human-readable title, such as `USGS Significant Earthquakes, Past Week`.

status.description: HTTP status the service assigned to the query, repeated inside the body.

api.description: Version of the service that answered, such as `2.7.0`.

count.description: Number of features in this document. Absent once `limit` is sent, which is why no pagination is declared; see the endpoint's notes.

limit.description: Row limit the query carried, echoed back. Present only when the query sent one.

offset.description: Row offset the query carried, echoed back. Present only when the query sent one.

features.description: One entry per earthquake, newest first unless the query asked otherwise.

bbox.title: BoundingBox
bbox.description: Bounding box of every feature in the document: minimum corner then maximum corner, each longitude, latitude, depth. Absent when the document holds no features, and on the event query.

EarthquakeFeature.title: EarthquakeFeature
EarthquakeFeature.description: One earthquake as a GeoJSON feature: where it was, and everything known about it.

id.description: Event id, the network code and the event code joined, such as `us6000m0xl`.

geometry.title: EarthquakePoint
geometry.description: Where the earthquake was, as a GeoJSON point.

coordinates.title: EpicenterCoordinates
coordinates.description: Longitude, latitude and depth, in that order. GeoJSON puts longitude first, and USGS uses the third position for depth in kilometres rather than the altitude GeoJSON nominally means.

prefixItems.title: longitude
prefixItems.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, negative west of the prime meridian.

prefixItems.title: latitude
prefixItems.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, negative south of the equator.

prefixItems.title: depth
prefixItems.description: Depth of the event below the surface, in kilometres. Negative for an event located above the surface.

EarthquakeProperties.title: EarthquakeProperties
EarthquakeProperties.description: What is known about one earthquake. Most fields are null until the contributing network has computed them.

mag.description: Magnitude, on the scale named by `magType`. Null before a magnitude has been computed.

place.description: Human-readable description of the location, relative to a named place.

updated.description: When this event's information was last updated, UTC.

tz.description: Time zone offset from UTC at the epicenter, in minutes. Deprecated by USGS and null on every current event.

url.description: Event page for a human reader.

detail.description: URL of this event's own GeoJSON document, which carries the products the summary leaves out.

felt.description: Number of "Did You Feel It?" responses. Null when nobody has reported one.

cdi.description: Maximum reported intensity, from "Did You Feel It?" responses.

mmi.description: Maximum estimated instrumental intensity, from ShakeMap.

alert.description: PAGER alert level, an estimate of the impact. Null until PAGER has run.

status.description: Whether a human has reviewed this event.

tsunami.description: 1 when the event is in a region with an active tsunami-warning system and large enough to matter, 0 otherwise. Not a tsunami warning.

sig.description: How significant the event is, 0 to 1000, from magnitude, felt reports and estimated impact.

net.description: Id of the network that contributed the preferred information, such as `us`.

code.description: Event code assigned by `net`, unique within that network.

ids.description: Every event id this event has been known by, comma-delimited with a leading and trailing comma.

sources.description: Every network that contributed to this event, comma-delimited with a leading and trailing comma.

types.description: Every product type associated with this event, comma-delimited with a leading and trailing comma.

nst.description: Number of seismic stations used to compute the location.

dmin.description: Horizontal distance from the epicenter to the nearest station, in degrees.

gap.description: Largest azimuthal gap between stations, in degrees; a smaller gap means a better-constrained location.

magType.description: Method used to compute `mag`, such as `mww`, `mb` or `ml`. Left a plain string: USGS lists the methods it uses today and adds to that list, so a `Literal` would reject a valid future response.

type.description: Kind of seismic event: `earthquake` for nearly all of them, and quarry blasts, explosions and ice quakes for the rest. A plain string for the same reason as `magType`.

title.description: Magnitude and place in one line, such as `M 7.5 - 2024 Noto Peninsula, Japan Earthquake`.
